---
title: "Lesson 6: Customizing your site"
---

All of these settings go in `_quarto.yml`. After changing them, preview to see the result.

## Themes, and light and dark mode

Quarto includes about two dozen free [Bootswatch themes](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html): `cosmo`, `flatly`, `litera`, `lumen`, `sandstone`, `yeti`, and more.

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: flatly
```

To offer a light and a dark version, with a toggle in the navbar:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: cosmo
      dark: darkly
    respect-user-color-scheme: true   # start in the reader's system setting
```

This is what the NV OSE training site uses.

## Logo, footer, and search

```yaml
website:
  title: "My Practice Site"
  search: true                      # search box in the navbar
  page-navigation: true             # "previous / next" buttons at the bottom of pages
  navbar:
    logo: images/logo.png
    logo-alt: "Organization logo"   # alt text for the logo
  page-footer:
    left: "My Organization"
    center: "Questions? Email [me@example.gov](mailto:me@example.gov)"
    right: "Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org)"
```

`logo` and `logo-alt` go **under `navbar:`**, not directly under `website:`.

## Small style tweaks with CSS

`styles.css` is for small adjustments. For example, to make the navbar logo sit on a white background in dark mode:

```css
.navbar-logo {
  background-color: #fff;
  border-radius: 4px;
  padding: 2px;
}
```

Keep CSS changes small. A theme does most of the work.

## Accessibility: make it usable for everyone

Public health sites should work for people using screen readers, keyboard navigation, or high contrast. Quarto handles much of this. You're responsible for:

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| **Alt text on every image and chart** | `{fig-alt="..."}` on images; `#| fig-alt:` on chunks |
| **Meaningful link text** | `[Download the report](...)`, not `[click here](...)` |
| **Headings in order** | `##` then `###`, without skipping levels; don't use headings just to make text big |
| **Readable contrast** | Text must stand out from its background (at least 4.5:1). Some theme elements don't, especially in dark mode. Check with a contrast tool, not by eye |
| **Email addresses as links** | `[me@example.gov](mailto:me@example.gov)` |
| **Don't rely on color alone** | In charts, use labels or line styles as well as color |

::: {.callout-tip title="Contrast fixes for cosmo and darkly"}
The NV OSE site's [`styles.css`](https://github.com/nv-ose/training/blob/main/styles.css) contains tested fixes for some low-contrast parts of these two themes (buttons, previous/next links, code in headings). Copy it if you use the same themes.
:::

## Copy buttons and table of contents

```yaml
format:
  html:
    toc: true                # "On this page" outline
    toc-title: "On this page"
    code-copy: true          # copy button on code blocks
    code-overflow: wrap      # wrap long code lines instead of scrolling
```
